clue.text: Ornament? Composer's almost room for one

indicators.note: for means one piece takes the place of another, here inside the composer's name

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the German composer
A is one, as in 'a book'

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether a composer's room has space for one more ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ROOM to ROO, and 'for' swaps that in for the A (one) in BACH.
explanation.definitionFit: A brooch is a pin-on piece of jewellery, a kind of personal decoration.

clue.text: I am dressing 24, holding up party

definitions.note: the setter, Puck, speaks: Puck is the other name of the Shakespearean sprite

parts.note: robing is putting on robes, so dressing

indicators.note: holding means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the answer to 24 across, a father, read as two words: old gives O and man gives FELLOW

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A setter describing getting dressed in a costume that restrains a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Puck, and the sprite Puck in A Midsummer Night's Dream is also called by this name. '24' is used for its two words split up, old and man, not as a whole; 'up' and 'holding' signal the reversal and insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle's setter signs as Puck, the mischievous sprite whose other folk name this is.

clue.text: Top boss? Mum mouths off: "Animal!"

indicators.note: mouths are the openings, so each word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A mother shouts insults at the head of the company, calling the boss an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouths off' takes the opening letter from each of Top, boss and Mum, leaving OP, OSS and UM.
explanation.definitionFit: The opossum is a marsupial mammal of the Americas, so an example of an animal.

clue.text: It's a frightful thing, almost struggling to walk without glasses on, initially

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the trimmed word goes round the other letters
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: hobbling is walking with difficulty

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of glasses and on are used

explanation.surface: Someone stumbling about without spectacles is a frightening sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' gives HOBBLIN, and 'without' (in the old sense of outside) wraps it round GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobgoblin is a mischievous imp or bogey from folklore, a thing to scare children.

clue.text: Uncovered aunt desperately lying about age? Just a little awkward

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters of aunt are stripped away
about means the anagrammed letters go round the extra letter
desperately signals the letters of lying are thrown into disorder
just a little of the word age means its first letter

explanation.surface: An aunt caught out fibbing about her age is a little embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' scrambles LYING to GINLY, and 'about' puts it round A, the first of age.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungainly means clumsy and lacking grace, a near synonym for awkward.

clue.text: Unruly youth, first out of bed, with hairstyle changed to latest version

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
DA, short for duck's arse, is a 1950s swept-back haircut
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a rebellious British youth of the 1950s

explanation.surface: A tearaway teenager gets up and has his hair restyled in the latest fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts UP at the front. A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style clothes, often wearing a DA haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Something updated has been revised or brought into its current form.

clue.text: Harsh-sounding brother

indicators.note: sounding says the word for harsh is heard, not seen

parts.note: grim means stern or harsh

explanation.surface: A brother whose voice comes across as severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob and Wilhelm, the Brothers Grimm, collected German fairy tales, so either is a brother.

clue.text: One that cuts new coins in Ireland

indicators.note: in means the scrambled letters sit inside the abbreviation
new means the letters of coins are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A tool or machine that stamps fresh coins in an Irish mint.
explanation.definitionFit: Incisors are the front teeth used for biting and slicing food.

clue.text: Someone like me to throw up a pork pie on the hearth?

parts.note: to lob is to throw something high in the air
pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie
the hearth is the floor in front of the fireplace, so beside the fire

explanation.surface: A setter imagines tossing a pork pie up onto the fireside.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie (or porky) is British rhyming slang for a lie. The setter, Puck, is a sprite, and this is a household sprite of English folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: This brownie-like household spirit of English folklore is a sprite, the same kind of creature as the setter's namesake.

clue.text: Something Arabs or Bedouin have imbibed

indicators.note: something of these words means a run of letters taken from within them

explanation.surface: Desert travellers have drunk something.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb is to take in or soak up, as one takes in a drink.

clue.text: Demons? Fashionable young reporter has one

parts.note: something in is in fashion
a cub reporter is a trainee journalist
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A trendy trainee journalist owns something.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi are male demons of legend that visit sleepers; the question mark flags the plural form.

clue.text: Made notes about animals

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round

parts.note: a singer has sung, producing musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone jotted down observations about wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made notes' looks like writing; it is singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildebeest, the antelopes of African plains, are a kind of animal.

clue.text: Upbeat current film has visual restraint

indicators.note: restraint means the word for visual holds the other pieces captive inside it

parts.note: optic means relating to the eye or sight
I is the symbol for electric current
a film of moisture is a mist

explanation.surface: A cheerful new movie shows admirable visual understatement.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat and this word both describe a hopeful, positive outlook.

clue.text: Stiff examination involving mark set by female

indicators.note: involving means the exam word wraps round the letter

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
M stands for mark, as in the old German currency

explanation.surface: A rigid test marked by a woman examiner.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff manners are starchy and ceremonious, as conduct that is very proper and correct.

clue.text: Paint picture of second bed in flower

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the river

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a crib is a child's bed

explanation.surface: Painting a second flowerbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' reads as a bloom but means a river, the Dee.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint a picture of something in words is to depict or portray it.

clue.text: Kills a little time at Angler's Rest, ultimately getting drunk

parts.note: S is short for second, a little time

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of rest is used
getting drunk means the letters reel about into a new order

parts.note: taken with the possessive s as a letter

explanation.surface: A pub called the Angler's Rest where a quick drinking session turns deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angler's Rest is the fictional pub of P G Wodehouse's Mr Mulliner stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle someone is to choke them to death, so this verb means kills.

clue.text: Was in contact with John Peel? Sorry, no idea about that

indicators.note: about means the anagrammed letters go round the abbreviation
sorry, as in a sorry state, signals the letters are in poor order

parts.note: John Peel was a famous BBC radio disc jockey, a DJ

explanation.surface: A puzzled reply when asked whether someone got in touch with the late broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel was a long-serving BBC Radio 1 DJ.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that adjoined were next to and touching each other.

clue.text: Eight in a row?

parts.note: a rowing eight is the crew of eight people in a racing boat, here seen in a row

explanation.surface: Eight items lined up consecutively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a line but is the verb to row.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing eight is crewed by eight rowers pulling oars in a race.

clue.text: Criminal activity of daughter somewhere in London

parts.note: Ealing is a district of west London

explanation.surface: A daughter's lawbreaking in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing is a borough of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Drug dealing is selling illegal drugs, an offence.

clue.text: Heartless men wrongly take over Times, heartlessly

parts.note: to rob is to take something unlawfully
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle of the word is removed, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: Cruel men unjustly seize control of a newspaper, acting without compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' looks like cruelty, but robots literally lack hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Robots are machines in human form with no heart, so men who are heartless in a literal way.

clue.text: Have to get in a cheesecake

indicators.note: to get in means the word for have goes inside the cheese

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese; the cake part of the word defines
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Someone has to fetch a cheesecake.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word cheesecake works twice: 'cheese' is BRIE, and 'cake' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownie is a small square of rich chocolate cake.

clue.text: Playing Puck not Bottom, learn he is a helpful creature

indicators.note: playing means the letters are toyed with into a new order
not bottom means the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: An actor cast as Puck rather than Bottom in the Dream learns he must be a helpful sprite.
explanation.walkthrough: Puck and Bottom are characters in A Midsummer Night's Dream; 'not Bottom' cuts the K from Puck.
explanation.definitionFit: This little Irish fairy of folklore is a sprite who may help or play tricks.

clue.text: Unable to love choral music

parts.note: unable to means can't
O is love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone who can't bring themselves to like choral music.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, canto is the melody or upper voice part, as in canto fermo for a choir.

clue.text: Insane woman's backing poet

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
's here means has: the words before it hold the hidden answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deranged woman supports a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters NEWO sit inside 'Insane woman's'; 'backing' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilfred Owen was the English First World War poet of Dulce et Decorum Est.

clue.text: Father of actor undergoing split

definitions.meaning: a father, in informal speech, is a dad
Gary ... the actor, his surname split into two words

explanation.surface: An actor's father is going through a break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The actor is Gary Oldman, whose surname splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, your dad or a husband is called this, a colloquial term for a male parent.

clue.text: After I left, floor covering is in a state

parts.note: lino, short for linoleum, is a floor covering

explanation.surface: Once I had left, the floor covering was in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' reads as messy; 'in' is a link and 'a state' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is one of the fifty US states, with Chicago its largest city.

clue.text: Final appearance of Desmond, N in Sunset Boulevard

parts.note: Norma Desmond, the faded star of the film Sunset Boulevard, was played by Gloria Swanson
N for Norma in the film was played by G for Gloria

explanation.surface: The last screen role of a star who played Norma Desmond in the 1950 film.
explanation.walkthrough: N. Desmond (Norma) in Sunset Boulevard was played by G. Swanson (Gloria); the clue swaps character for actress.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan song is a farewell performance, from the legend that a swan sings just before dying.

clue.text: Female king? The Spanish are ready

definitions.note: the ready is slang for money, a noun

parts.note: she is a female pronoun
K is the chess abbreviation for king
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A queen and a Spanish group declare themselves prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' looks like an adjective but is slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The shekel is the currency of Israel, so a form of cash or money.
